children.description:
1) Programa Tu Oportunidad: During 2022, SCE Chile launched a new evidence-based methodology (based on the results of a previously developed pilot program), with two learning routes, one towards entrepreneurship and the other towards employability, depending to the participant’s profile (beginner/advanced). This methodology was implemented by the AIEP, a renown technical education institute, that undertook the mission to address the economic empowerment of women, migrants, and indigenous people with socioeconomic vulnerability through a sustainable model for technical education in this area. In addition, this institution is leveraging its vast network of private and public actors to increase opportunities for participants through referrals to entrepreneurship and employment clusters. As part of its sustainability program its community of students and graduates are encouraged to engage in volunteering activities.  There are currently 6,476 women participating in this program and 1,660 have been mentored by the 140 volunteer mentors who belong to the Your Opportunity Mentor Network. Another 542 women have been trained to become mentors to other SCE women as well as agents of change in their communities.  In terms of impact, and according to the follow-up survey of graduates three and six months after graduating, 37% of women improved their income; 16% of women found employment; 20% returned to formal education; 24% started a new business; 36% improved the business they already had; and 44% continued their education, all thanks to the AIEP program.
The AIEP program also strengthened its regional and national partnerships, identifying opportunities for collaborative projects and establishing labor reference protocols with the Ministry of the Interior, local governments and civil society organizations. Specifically in the northern region of the country, partnerships for the implementation of programmes and linkages have been strengthened (including SERNAMEG - National Women's Service, and SECREDUC - Regional Education Agency). More importantly, SCE Chile has been actively involved in the IOM/UNHCR-led roundtable on migration. In the southern zone, alliances have been developed in the Magallanes Region (including SERNAMEG, INDAP - National Institute of Agricultural Development, Venezuelans in Patagonia and other civil society institutions) to include more women from the most remote areas of the country. Simultaneously, SCE Chile has advanced in developing new partnerships with institutions and agencies for this new period of implementation (Ministry of Social Development,  INJUV, University of La Frontera and civil society).
In addition, SCE Chile led the public-private roundtable "More women in STEM education" which was developed jointly with Fundación País Digital (funded and supported by TELCOs and Technology companies in Chile) facilitating discussion among civil society actors, companies, universities and government to provide critical inputs and a gender approach for public policies in STEM education. Finally, SCE Chile prepared and disseminated a policy  report on Second Chance Education with a Gender Perspective with good practices and recommendations, contributing to public policy on online education and training for adult women.
2) Programa Originarias: During 2022, UN Women through its Originarias Programme contributed to the economic and social empowerment of more than 1,000 indigenous women in Chile, contributing towards the achievement of Sustainable Development Goals 1, 4, 5, 8, 12 and 17 of the 2030 Agenda and the strategic priorities of economic integration, education for work, citizen participation and effective exercise of human rights of the United Nations Cooperation Framework for Sustainable Development in Chile 2019-2022. 
Training and technical assistance provided by UN Women in conjunction with indigenous facilitators and academic and state institutions enabled more than 1,000 indigenous women to strengthen their leadership and advocacy skills, and more than 400 indigenous women entrepreneurs to access services, goods and resources, improving their opportunities for economic integration and participation in decision-making. 
The strategy implemented to actively train and promote the participation of indigenous trainers in intercultural learning spaces was a key factor for the success of the Originarias Program. The facilitators of the Originarias Program are mostly indigenous women (95%) who were trained in UN Women Training of Trainers schools. During 2012, these women, through the Originarias Program, participated in learning opportunities aimed at non-indigenous youth and adults and contributed to facilitate dialogues between indigenous women to elaborate proposals for economic development agendas. Finally, within the framework of the exercise of cultural rights, the program developed a school to improve the Aymara language skills of 28 intercultural educators, benefitting indirectly more than 4,000 indigenous children in the Tarapacá region.
As a result of the impacts generated by the Originarias Program, during 2022 a new donation agreement was signed with Teck Resources Ltd. for a total of 5.25 million dollars, which will enable the implementation of a 5-year process that will escalate over the years to incorporate new management strategies and financing mechanisms, to increasing the benefits  resulting from the Original Program and make these sustainable in the long term, placing the responsibility of strategic development on indigenous women themselves. With a proven methodology for empowerment, based on the integration of a rights, gender perspective and interculturality approach, the Originarias Program has the potential to be replicated in other territories, within Chile and in Latin America.
3) Proyecto Recuperación económica MPTF: Under the framework of the successful implementation of the MPTF program, UN Women during 2022 reached and established strategic alliances with many sectors of society (public, private, civil society, and communities), facilitating the  progress in different areas of gender equality, providing tools to improve women's economic opportunities, promoting leadership of micro-entrepreneur women, working with their businesses to include a gender perspective in their operation, raising awareness in the population in care co-responsibility issues, and generating information to guide the design of local and global policies.
One significant outcome of the program is related to the partnerships and collaboration networks that were created during its implementation and are still in place after the project's conclusion. The coordination of networks with different sectors and actors, the private and public sectors, employers and workers organizations, civil society, communities, and other initiatives from the UN, were crucial for creating better economic opportunities for women from the sectors most affected by the pandemic (heads of the household, migrants, women from rural areas, and caregivers). The MujeresEmplea.org virtual platform consolidated the offer of work and training opportunities, access to funds, and subsidies to entrepreneurship and care services (with more than 100 updated publications), with more than 67,000 visits during the implementation period. In parallel, the Activa Empresarias platform was created to connect the demand of products and services of large companies with the supply of companies led by women. 
A pilot training, mentoring, and community care services program was successfully designed and implemented. It positively impacted the insertion of women into the labor market. It allowed their economic activation mainly in three communes of Chile with high female social vulnerability rates (Renca, Padre las Casas, and San Pedro de Atacama). More than 9,000 women were trained in digital skills for employment and/or entrepreneurship, and more than 350 women were mentored for their labor insertion. The job fairs for women offered more than 33,000 job openings, to which more than 3,000 women applied. 
The childcare service was available in the selected territories to facilitate the access of their caregivers to training and work opportunities, providing care to 125 children per day.
A network of 300 women was trained and certified in care services, laying the foundations to establish a national caregiver's network, which the Government of Chile is currently promoting.
Awareness-raising and promoting care co-responsibility had a great reach among companies in the selected territories and the general population, promoting gender equality through communication plans and workshops designed for each target audience.

children.description:
En el marco de la COP 25 bajo la presidencia de Chile, el país asumió el compromiso de profundizar en la agenda de género y la acción climática.  Para ello firmó acuerdo de colaboración con el Gran Ducado de Luxemburgo para implementar el proyecto “Género y cambio climático”, implementado por l Sistema de las Naciones Unidas y el Ministerio de Medio Ambiente.  En este proyecto, participaron el Programa de las Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo (PNUD) y la Organización de las Naciones Unidas para la Alimentación y la Agricultura (FAO) y ONU Mujeres que lideró la ejecución del proyecto. El Éxito del proyecto, implicó que, en base a los resultados y lecciones aprendidas de esta iniciativa, que el Gran Ducado de Luxemburgo, decidiera apoyar por 4 años, a partir de 2023, una iniciativa regional, liderada por la Oficina Regional de ONU Mujeres, sobre cambio climático y enfoque de género. Los antecedentes y resultados del proyecto son los siguientes:

El objetivo principal del proyecto fue generar información que permita incorporar el enfoque de género en las políticas, programas y planes nacionales sectoriales de cambio climático. 

Para lograr el objetivo, se propuso generar información estadística e indicadores que den cuenta de las brechas de género existentes y permitan contar con datos desagregados para una mejor, eficiente y justa toma de decisiones, priorizando las áreas más urgente para reducir las desigualdades y el impacto medioambiental. Se crearon indicadores y un plan de monitoreo insertos en los planes nacionales de Adaptación y Mitigación, junto con programas específicos de género que considerearon el factor climático. Finalmente, la información obtenida fue puesta a disposición pública a través de la plataforma ARClim , visibilizando la distribución de las desigualdades por género, edad y territorio de la población desde el punto de vista climático.

En segundo lugar, al considerar la poca evidencia sobre la efectividad de programas existentes   en torno a género y cambio climático, el proyecto hizo hincapié en la importancia de incluir la perspectiva de género en las políticas sobre esta materia, dando a conocer y compartiendo avances sobre aquellas implementadas en el resto del mundo. 

En tercer lugar, el proyecto también propuso fortalecer las capacidades para una transversalización de género en temáticas ambientales, de funcionarios y funcionarias del Ministerio de Medio Ambiente, sociedad civil, academia y quienes toman decisiones a nivel nacional y regional. Ello, a través de capacitaciones, charlas y cursos especializados en Género y Medio Ambiente, con el fin de generar habilidades y conocimientos valiosos que ayuden a impulsar la inclusión de una perspectiva de género en las decisiones, programas y políticas medioambientales, así como también en el diálogo ciudadano. 

En relación a los avances, a nivel nacional se integró el enfoque de género en su Contribución Determinada a nivel Nacional (CDN), se presentó la Estrategia Climática de Largo Plazo (ECLP) con metas asociadas a la equidad e igualdad de género;  con el fin de generar conocimiento frente a los efectos diferenciados del cambio climático, se conformó una Mesa de Género y Cambio Climático de carácter intersectorial y se elaboraron cinco instrumentos además de integrar y complementar estas nuevas herramientas con otras iniciativas desarrolladas por el Ministerio de Medio Ambiente de Chile, en el país y la Región, como el Manual de Gestión para la Integración del enfoque de género en la acción climática, la Lista de Chequeo para integrar género en los instrumentos de cambio climático; y el estudio Generación de indicadores y análisis sectorial sobre género y cambio climático en cuatro sectores vulnerables al cambio climático: ciudades, pesca y acuicultura, biodiversidad y agricultura, modelo innovador y que servirá de base para apoyar a los distintos sectores que en el plazo de 2 años deben elaborar un plan de acción con enfoque de género en respuesta la reciente Ley Marco de Cambio climático.

children.name: Actividades del  PLAN DE GESTIÓN DE ELIMINACIÓN DE HCFC (II)
children.description:
En la 76ª Reunión del Comité Ejecutivo del Fondo Multilateral del Protocolo de Montreal se aprobaron fondos como parte de la Etapa II del Plan de Gestión de Eliminación de HCFC en Chile (HPMP-II) en Chile, para la implementación del componente de Servicios y Mantenimiento de el sector de la refrigeración y el aire acondicionado. Este componente es implementado por la Unidad Nacional de Ozono del Ministerio del Ambiente en coordinación con ONUDI.

En coordinación con el Gobierno de Chile, el sector industrial y ONUDI, se diseñó una estrategia para la eliminación de los HCFC utilizados en el sector de refrigeración y aire acondicionado, con el objetivo de ayudar al país a cumplir con las metas establecidas en el Protocolo de Montreal y por el Comité Ejecutivo del MP para 2020 y 2021, con base en las prioridades ya establecidas por el Gobierno para la Etapa II.

children.name: Actividades del  PLAN DE GESTIÓN DE ELIMINACIÓN DE HCFC (III)
children.description:
La Fase III del plan de gestión de eliminación de HCFC contiene cuatro líneas estratégicas, dentro de las cuales se encuentran la Línea Estratégica #2: “Programa de apoyo al sector de refrigeración y aire acondicionado” y la Línea Estratégica #4 “Programa de Monitoreo”, que incluyen las siguientes actividades:

1. Capacitación en mejores prácticas de refrigeración y aire acondicionado, y certificación de mujeres técnicas en habilidades RAC, para mejorar la gestión de HCFC y sus alternativas, reduciendo las emisiones al medio ambiente.
2. Asistencia técnica al sector RAC, a través del Programa Cero Fugas, para la realización de proyectos piloto en sistemas frigoríficos revisando y controlando sus fugas, consumo energético, consumos de refrigerante, para mejorar sus parámetros de rendimiento.
3. Asistencia técnica para los centros de recuperación, para mejorar su operación y capacidades de control de calidad para refrigerantes regenerados: y
4. Supervisión de la ejecución de las actividades del plan de gestión de eliminación de HCFC-III.
